title: Kingdom of Bamum founded
description: Nchare Yen founds the Bamum kingdom in the Grassfields, a state whose kings later create a unique script and resist both the Germans and the French.

title: Portuguese name the Wouri 'River of Prawns'
description: Portuguese sailors reach the coast and, finding the estuary full of prawns, call it Rio dos Camarões, which becomes the country's name.

title: Mandara kingdom founded
description: The Wandala set up a kingdom in the mountains south of Lake Chad that endures as a strong Muslim state until the colonial era.

title: Adamawa Emirate founded
description: Modibo Adama, campaigning with a flag from Usman dan Fodio, founds a Fulani emirate that rules the highlands later called the Adamawa.

title: Kamerun becomes a German protectorate
description: After Gustav Nachtigal secures treaties with the Duala kings, Germany proclaims its protectorate of Kamerun.

title: Neukamerun added
description: Ending the Agadir Crisis, France cedes large parts of its Congo colonies to Germany as 'Neukamerun', with the lands returned under the new war in 1916.

title: Germany loses Kamerun
description: The last German garrison surrenders at Mora after an eighteen-month campaign, and Britain and France divide the colony between them.

title: League mandates divide Cameroon
description: League of Nations mandates confirm the wartime partition: France takes the larger east and Britain two strips on the Nigerian border.

title: UPC revolt begins
description: The French administration bans the nationalist Union of the Peoples of Cameroon after riots, and the party's armed revolt burns on past independence.

title: Ruben Um Nyobé killed
description: French troops track down and kill the UPC's leader in the Sanaga bush, but the guerrilla war he led is largely written out of official memory.

title: Independence from France
description: French Cameroun becomes independent with Ahmadou Ahidjo as president.

title: British Cameroons plebiscite
description: The northern strip of the British mandate votes to join Nigeria and the southern districts to join Cameroon.

title: Reunification creates a federal republic
description: Southern Cameroons joins the Republic of Cameroon as West Cameroon, forming a federal republic in English and French.

title: One-party state
description: Ahidjo folds the parties of both states into his Cameroon National Union, leaving a single ruling party.

title: Federation abolished
description: A referendum ends the federal system and creates the unitary United Republic of Cameroon.

title: Biya succeeds Ahidjo
description: Ahidjo resigns without warning and Prime Minister Paul Biya takes over, beginning a presidency that lasts for decades.

title: Coup attempt against Biya
description: Republican Guard soldiers of the northern old guard try to overthrow Biya and are crushed after days of fighting.

title: Lake Nyos disaster
description: A cloud of carbon dioxide bursts from the crater lake and suffocates some 1,700 people in the villages below.

title: Social Democratic Front launched
description: An opposition party launches in Bamenda despite a ban and police fire that kills six, and multiparty politics returns.

title: Bakassi awarded to Cameroon
description: The International Court of Justice awards the oil-rich Bakassi peninsula to Cameroon, settling a dispute that had brought armed clashes with Nigeria.

title: Nigeria hands over Bakassi
description: Under the Greentree Agreement Nigeria formally transfers the peninsula.

title: Anglophone Crisis begins
description: Strikes by anglophone lawyers and teachers meet a harsh response and grow into an armed separatist conflict.
